text: - Records Access and the Service Junction now have real doors, approved by Nathanial Henniges from rendered frames. You come into Records Access through a steel swing door that its closer swings shut behind you, and you leave through another: securing the first copy in the dark security container beside the exit lets the exit's bolt go, its lamp turns amber and the door swings open on its hinges, then the engineer walks out through it with WOLF following. The Service Junction's entry is the same kind of door. Its sealed door is now a steel blast door in a concrete wall across the walkway, with a lamp on the wall's near column (red, amber while the line builds, flashing red and white while the fuse burns, steady red with REDUCED MOTION); when it blows it is torn off its hinges and thrown along the floor, where it lands and lies, and you walk through the doorway behind its column. The exit is a sliding steel door in the wall at the room's right end: popping the bolt slides it into its pocket, WOLF steps into the doorway and waits, and you leave from the door itself (from the EXIT BOLT box, which now stands a little further from it, the hint only says it is open). On leaving, WOLF walks out through it first and the engineer follows him before the END OF SLICE card; nobody fades out. Through the open exit the coolant line runs on along the passage beyond. The doors replace the earlier pressure bulkhead and hatch images; their art was made with AI assistance, painted inside shapes drawn by scripts from real door hardware. Checked by automated tests, a new one among them that walks the route through every door, and by still images from scripted play at 1280x720 and on a 1920x1080 touch layout; not played by hand, so the thrown door and the walk-outs have not been seen in motion.

text: - The door end of the maintenance corridor gains the additions Nathanial Henniges approved.
